vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openserv-agent-sdk
Version: 1.0.1

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle for the OpenServ Agent SDK is benign. It provides a framework and examples for building AI agents, including capabilities for LLM interaction, task management, file operations within a workspace, and Web3 integration (ERC-8004 on-chain identity, x402 payments). All observed network calls are to expected OpenServ platform endpoints (e.g., `agents-proxy.openserv.ai`) or legitimate third-party services (e.g., `openai.com`). Sensitive environment variables like `WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY` are handled for legitimate platform authentication and Web3 transactions, with clear documentation on their purpose and usage. There is no evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms beyond the agent's operational needs, or prompt injection against the AI agent itself designed to cause harm. The instructions and code align with the stated purpose of developing and deploying AI agents.

llm.summary: The SDK appears to match its stated purpose (building OpenServ agents), but the runtime instructions ask for and write sensitive credentials (wallet private key, platform API key/auth token, LLM keys) while the skill metadata declares no required environment variables — this mismatch and the credential persistence behavior merit caution before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: The skill is an SDK for building/deploying agents and the included examples and docs align with that purpose. It references the companion openserv-client package (expected). However, the metadata declares no required environment variables while the SKILL.md clearly documents use of and automatic population of sensitive env vars (WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY, OPENSERV_API_KEY, OPENSERV_AUTH_TOKEN, plus optional LLM keys). That omission in the metadata is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs code to call provision(), which will create or reuse a wallet, register the agent, and write credentials into the environment. It also documents capabilities that can upload/delete files and post logs to tasks. These behaviors are coherent for an agent SDK but involve creation, storage and use of sensitive credentials and network-exposed tunnels. The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated host files, but they do imply persistent credential writes and opening network endpoints — both sensitive operations that should be reviewed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec). The SKILL.md recommends installing npm packages from the public registry (@openserv-labs/*, zod, openai, etc.), which is expected for a TypeScript SDK. No arbitrary download URLs or archive extraction are specified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The env vars the docs reference (OPENAI_API_KEY, WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY, OPENSERV_API_KEY, OPENSERV_AUTH_TOKEN, PORT, tunnel flags) are relevant to running agents but the skill metadata lists none — a discrepancy. The SDK's provision() behavior (creating a wallet and writing a private key and platform auth creds into env/.env) is particularly sensitive and should be understood before use. Requiring or auto-creating private keys and tokens is proportionate to a platform-sdk, but it requires explicit disclosure in metadata and caution from the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true and does not change model-invocation flags (defaults allow invocation when eligible). That is typical for an SDK skill. However, because the SDK instructs code that will persist credentials (and may run a tunnel/exposed HTTP server), any automated invocation in an environment with credentials present could perform network actions using those creds — users should ensure they run such code only in controlled environments.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or running this SDK: 1) Inspect the example code (provision(), run(agent), file upload/delete, task APIs) to confirm you understand what will run. 2) Treat WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY and OPENSERV_* credentials as highly sensitive — do not run provision() on a machine with other valuable keys or in an untrusted environment. 3) Prefer creating an isolated dev environment (container or VM) and a throwaway wallet/account when you try this. 4) Validate the npm packages (@openserv-labs/sdk and client) origin and review their source if possible before npm install. 5) Rotate any auto-generated keys and do not commit .env files to version control. 6) Note the metadata omission (no declared env vars) — ask the publisher to correct it or provide a provenance/homepage before trusting the package in production.
